steps: Wash and slice the strawberries and slice the banana into rounds.
Spoon half the greek yogurt into a bowl or glass.
Add a layer of granola, half the strawberries and the blueberries.
Add the remaining yogurt and top with the rest of the granola, the strawberries and the banana.
Drizzle with the honey and serve immediately.

note: Relabeled American - a yogurt parfait is a US diner and health-food format, and nothing about layered granola is Mediterranean; Greek yogurt in the name is an ingredient, not a cuisine. Dropped the raw Rolled Oats, which were sitting dry in a cold parfait doing the same job as the granola, and raised the granola to compensate. One texture instead of two competing ones.

steps: Season the chicken breast with salt, black pepper and half the oregano and grill it, then slice it.
Dice the tomato, cucumber and bell pepper into rough chunks and thinly slice the red onion.
Tear the romaine lettuce.
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil, the lemon juice and the remaining oregano.
Top with the sliced chicken and the feta in a slab rather than crumbled, the way a horiatiki is served.

note: Relabeled Greek - the name says Greek and this is a horiatiki with chicken, not a generic Mediterranean bowl. Added the tomato and bell pepper it was missing, which are two of the four defining vegetables of a Greek salad, and cut the romaine back since a horiatiki is not a lettuce salad. No olives anywhere, per the standing constraint - they would be traditional here and are deliberately left out.

steps: Dice the onion, carrot and potato and mince the garlic.
Brown the ground lamb in the olive oil in a heavy pot, breaking it up.
Add the onion, garlic and carrot and cook 2 minutes, then stir in the cumin and toast it 30 seconds - blooming the cumin in the fat is what gives the soup its depth.
Add the red lentils, the diced potato, the tomato sauce and about 1 1/2 cups of water. Stir to combine.
Simmer 25-30 minutes until the lentils have collapsed and the potato is tender. Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve hot.

note: Steps only, no ingredient change. Two real bugs fixed: the cooking liquid was a flat 3 cups against 33 g of dry lentils, now about 1 1/2 cups, and the cumin was never bloomed in the fat - it is now toasted with the aromatics rather than dropped into liquid.

steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions.
Cube the sweet potato, toss it with half the olive oil, salt and black pepper, and roast at 200C for 25 minutes until caramelised at the edges.
Season the chicken breast and grill or pan-sear it, then slice it.
Wilt the spinach briefly.
Build the bowl with the rice, sweet potato, chicken and spinach, and dress it with the remaining olive oil.

note: Relabeled American - 'power bowl' is a Californian health-food genre and brown rice with roasted sweet potato belongs to it, not to any Mediterranean tradition. Oil raised 8 to 12 g and split explicitly between roasting and dressing; at 8 g there was not enough for both and the finishing drizzle was fictional.

steps: Boil the potato until tender, then slice it while still warm.
Blanch the green beans 3 minutes and drop them into ice water.
Soft-boil the egg 7 minutes, peel and halve it.
Season the ahi tuna with salt and black pepper and sear it 1 minute per side, leaving it rare in the middle, then slice it.
Cut the tomato into wedges.
Whisk the olive oil with the red wine vinegar and a little salt and pepper into a dressing.
Arrange the potato, green beans, egg and tomato on a plate, lay the tuna over, and spoon the dressing across. No olives, by preference.

note: Relabeled French - salade nicoise is from Nice and is one of the most fiercely defended regional dishes there is. Added tomato, which is non-negotiable in any version. Took the report's option (a) and treated the ahi as the fresh steak it actually is, with an explicit searing step, rather than pretending it was tinned. Added a vinaigrette - the salad previously had oil and no acid. Olives are traditional and are deliberately omitted per the standing constraint; the step says so plainly rather than silently.

steps: Brown the ground lamb with the cumin, paprika, salt and black pepper, then squeeze the lemon over it off the heat.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and thinly slice the red onion.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan.
Spread the hummus across the tortilla, lay the spinach over it, then the lamb, tomato, cucumber and red onion.
Roll it up tightly and serve.

note: The report classed this as coherent with minor drift, and the one change that matters is the lemon squeezed over the lamb at the end - spiced lamb with no acid is flat. Swapped the carrot for tomato and added red onion, which is the standard raw component of a wrap in this idiom. Macro-neutral.

steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions.
Halve the bell peppers and remove the seeds.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Brown the ground beef with them until the onion is soft.
Mix the cooked rice into the beef with half the tomato sauce, the cumin, oregano, dried parsley, salt and black pepper.
Stuff the pepper halves with the mixture and top with the remaining tomato sauce.
Bake at 190C for 30 minutes, scattering the feta over for the last 5 minutes.

note: Added the onion and garlic the filling had none of - browning mince with neither is the clearest sign of an underbuilt stuffing. Doubled the tomato sauce so there is enough to bind the filling and top the peppers, which is how the moisture gets in. servingSize corrected from '2 peppers' to '2 stuffed halves', which is what 200 g of bell pepper and the steps actually describe.

steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions.
Sear the shrimp in a little of the olive oil, 2 minutes per side, until just pink. Season with salt and black pepper.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and thinly slice the red onion.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice and the oregano.
Toss the rice, vegetables and shrimp with the dressing and crumble the feta over the top.

note: Feta cut from 80 to 50 g - at 80 g against 120 g of shrimp the cheese outweighed the seafood and dominated a dish named for both. Added tomato and red onion, which is what the plate was missing, and raised the oil so there is enough to sear the shrimp AND dress the salad; at 10 g the dressing step was fictional.

steps: Cut the chicken breast into cubes and marinate them with the olive oil, the lemon juice, half the minced garlic, the oregano, paprika, salt and black pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the chicken onto skewers - souvlaki means little skewer, and the cubes-on-a-stick form is the dish.
Grill 12-15 minutes, turning, until charred at the edges.
Grate the cucumber and squeeze the liquid out of it, then stir it into the greek yogurt with the rest of the garlic and the dill to make tzatziki.
Dice the tomato and thinly slice the red onion.
Warm the pita and serve the skewers with the tzatziki, tomato and red onion.

note: Relabeled Greek. The component error the report flagged: the yogurt and cucumber were sitting on the plate as separate items when they are supposed to be combined into tzatziki, which needs the cucumber grated and squeezed dry or it turns to water. Cucumber raised so there is enough for the sauce and the plate, tomato added, and Dill (a Phase A spice name) added since tzatziki without it is just garlic yogurt. Also made the skewering explicit, since that is what the word means.

steps: Drain the canned tuna well and flake it into a bowl.
Rinse and drain the white beans and add them.
Dice the cucumber and thinly slice the red onion.
Dress with the olive oil, the lemon juice, the oregano, dried parsley, salt and black pepper, and fold gently so the beans keep their shape.
Serve with the whole wheat bread.

note: Fixes a phantom the audit did not catch and my own sweep did: step 1 said to drain tuna while the ingredient was Ahi Tuna, a fresh steak. Canned Tuna is a Phase A registry row and resolves it honestly. White beans raised from 19 to 60 g, which is what turns this from a garnish into fagioli e tonno - the beans should be a real portion. Dropped the low-carb tag, which was already wrong and is now clearly so.

steps: Mix the ground lamb with half the minced garlic, the cumin, oregano, salt and black pepper and knead it until it turns sticky and paste-like.
Press the seasoned lamb into a thin loaf and cook it in a hot skillet 3-4 minutes per side, then rest it and slice it thinly across - a gyro is shaved slices off a loaf, not crumbles.
Grate the cucumber and squeeze it dry, then stir it into the greek yogurt with the rest of the garlic and the lemon juice to make tzatziki.
Dice the tomato and thinly slice the red onion.
Warm the pita, spread the tzatziki over it, and fill with the sliced lamb, the tomato and the red onion.

note: The worst recipe in the slice: a Lamb Gyro containing 60 g of chicken breast alongside 60 g of lamb, with the chicken making up half the protein. Removed the chicken and doubled the lamb, so the name and the contents agree. Also fixed the technique - the lamb is now pressed into a loaf, cooked and sliced thin, rather than crumbled, since crumbled mince in a pita is a kofta. Tomato added and the tzatziki actually assembled. Relabeled Greek.

steps: Cut the potato into thick wedges and toss them with half the olive oil, half the lemon juice, the oregano, salt and black pepper.
Season the chicken breast and sear it in the remaining olive oil with the sliced red onion and the minced garlic until the onion softens.
Move the chicken and onion into a roasting dish with the potato wedges and pour the rest of the lemon juice over.
Roast at 190C for 40 minutes, basting once, until the potatoes have absorbed the lemon and gone golden at the edges.
Wilt the spinach and serve it alongside.

note: Relabeled Greek - this is kotopoulo lemonato and the name is already the English of a specific dish. Brown rice replaced with lemon-roasted potatoes, which is what the dish is served with; rice was the one component that made it read as generic. Oil doubled so there is enough to coat the potatoes and sear the chicken. The red onion is now cooked with the chicken rather than sitting raw and unexplained.

steps: Season the ahi tuna generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat a little of the olive oil in a heavy pan until almost smoking and sear the tuna 1-2 minutes per side, leaving the centre rare.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the minced garlic, the lemon juice and the oregano into a dressing.
Slice the tuna across the grain, plate it with the spinach and the sliced cucumber, and spoon the dressing over.

note: The report passed this as coherent and correctly labelled; the only real defect was that 5 g of olive oil had to both sear a 170 g steak and become a lemon-garlic dressing, so the dressing did not exist. Oil raised to 12 g and split explicitly between the two jobs, with oregano added to the dressing.

Clean - the report's only coherent-with-no-findings recipe in the slice. Every ingredient is referenced by a step, no phantoms, nothing unused, and the cuisine label is right. Deliberately left untouched.

blocked.did: OMITTED per the standing no-olives constraint. Both step lists now say so plainly rather than quietly leaving them out.

blocked.recipe: Mediterranean Tuna Salad / Tuna Nicoise Salad
blocked.wanted: Canned Tuna, flagged by the report as a recommended new registry entry
blocked.did: it IS in the registry - Phase A added it. Used it for Mediterranean Tuna Salad, which resolves a real phantom (the step said 'drain the tuna' while the ingredient was fresh Ahi Tuna). Tuna Nicoise keeps fresh ahi with an explicit searing step, the report's option (a).

blocked.wanted: Water 350g added to the ingredient list
blocked.did: not added - SPEC forbids Water in an ingredients array. The volume is stated proportionally in the step text instead.

_summary.notes: Written inline by the main session after the slice-07 agent was killed by a session limit before writing anything. 13 of 14 changed; Baked Cod with Lemon & Herbs is clean and untouched. No renames. Six cuisine relabels: 4 to Greek (Greek Chicken Salad, Chicken Souvlaki Plate, Lamb Gyro, Greek Lemon Chicken), 2 to American (Greek Yogurt Parfait, Brown Rice Power Bowl), 1 to French (Tuna Nicoise Salad). NOTE: Greek and French-for-nicoise mean Greek is a NEW cuisine label beyond the five pre-approved ones - flagged alongside Moroccan from slice 09. Mediterranean drops from 14 recipes to 7, which is the point: it was a catch-all hiding specific national dishes.
